identity.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR observation resolves to the Marcos Mantara LM600 race-car family. PMR's N-GT label is simulator taxonomy; PMR's own history places the modeled context in the early 2000s and mentions a 2000 British GT1 win. Period records also show LM600s in LM GT2 and a 1999 FIA homologation, so the exact PMR chassis and year remain unpinned. The evidence supports six forward gears and includes a sequential six-speed race configuration, but it also documents a different homologated LM600 configuration with a ZF synchronized manual gearbox. No reviewed source establishes the exact shift interface, clutch technique, shift electronics, or original steering-wheel geometry for the PMR target.

PMR's official car page names Marcos Mantara LM600 and lists a six-speed sequential transmission. Its dated history article places the modeled historical context in the early 2000s and specifically mentions a 2000 British GT1 result. The 1997 Le Mans record identifies an exact Mantara LM600 chassis with a Hewland sequential six-speed, while the FIA GT010 homologation form identifies the same model and documents a separate ZF six-speed manual/synchronized configuration. The repository contains no existing curated record for this identity, so a new record is proposed with the variant boundary made explicit.
